clue.text: Take it power cut is to continue

indicators.note: cut says a letter is removed from the word before it

parts.note: to take it (that something is so) is to presume it
P is the standard symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A strange instruction about accepting a blackout and carrying on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' takes P out of PRESUME. 'is to' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up again after a pause is to carry on, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Bird being studied heard before dawn

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: read, in the past tense, means studied
the dawn of something is its start

explanation.surface: A bird watched and listened to just before daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: Past-tense READ sounds like RED; 'before' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird of the thrush family with a rusty-red tail.

clue.text: More than just a few cut, almost all

parts.note: to sever is to cut

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of all is dropped

explanation.surface: More than a handful were cut, nearly all in fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Some number above two or three but not many, a quantity word.

clue.text: Male hanging around to enjoy carnival

indicators.note: around means the hanging goes round the word for enjoy

parts.note: an arras is a tapestry wall hanging
to dig something is slang for enjoying it

explanation.surface: A man loitering about to have a good time at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging around' reads as loitering; here 'hanging' is a tapestry noun and 'around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shrove Tuesday festival celebrated with parades, as in New Orleans.

clue.text: Letter opener for post — share with another

parts.note: the letter W is pronounced and spelt out as double-u

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, here of post

explanation.surface: Using a letter opener on the mail, then going halves with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter opener' reads as a paper knife, but 'Letter' is W spelt out as DOUBLE U, and 'opener for post' gives P.
explanation.definitionFit: To pair up and share something, such as a room or a seat, with someone else.

clue.text: Gradually ease temptation in resort

indicators.note: re-sort means sort again, so the letters of ease temptation are reordered

explanation.surface: Advice to give in to temptation slowly while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday spot but is read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Proceeding slowly, by small stages, an idiom for little by little.

clue.text: Short account covering a southern herb

indicators.note: covering means the shortened account goes round the other letters
short means the last letter of the account is dropped

parts.note: a bill is an account of what is owed

explanation.surface: A brief statement that includes a southern herb.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant culinary plant, a common example of the category.

clue.text: Passage coming from another court

parts.note: an extra is one more, another

explanation.surface: A corridor leading from one courtyard to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' looks like a corridor but is a piece taken from a book; 'coming from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A quoted excerpt from a text is a passage of it.

clue.text: In favour of exercises prior to run? Correct

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
PE is physical education, school exercises
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Is warming up before a run the right thing to do?
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting and right, as in the proper way to do things.

clue.text: Agreement in writing

definitions.meaning: a close match or similarity between things

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both close match between things and the letters people send each other.

clue.text: Daughter having no more, only fish

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies
something over is finished, no more
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: A daughter with nothing left but a fish to her name.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish of the English Channel, a named species of the general class.

clue.text: Start argument

definitions.meaning: to begin work eagerly, as in the phrase 'they started in'
a quarrel or brief fight, written with a hyphen as a noun

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means begin in earnest; as a hyphenated noun it means a scrap or row.

clue.text: Row involving stray dog

indicators.note: involving means the row takes the stray inside it

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats in a theatre
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A quarrel over a stray dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is a tier of seats; 'involving' puts ERR after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed type of small dog, originally bred to go to earth after badgers and foxes.

clue.text: Husbandry up to the time of decline

parts.note: till means until, up to the time of something
to age is to decline with the years

explanation.surface: Farming seen as a story running right up to a period of decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry is farming, and the cultivation of land by ploughing is a part of it.

clue.text: Person in charge lost, initially, in street in Paris by river

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the French street

parts.note: rue is French for street

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of lost is used

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A boss who has got lost on a Parisian street beside the Seine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign or governor is one who holds authority over others.

clue.text: Split peas, absurd price

indicators.note: absurd suggests the letters of peas are in a ridiculous order

parts.note: a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A greengrocer's complaint: split peas at a ridiculous price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like an adjective for the peas but is the verb definition; 'absurd' yields SEPA.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to divide or break apart, matching split.

clue.text: Manage diocese in spot echoing decline

parts.note: to run is to manage

indicators.note: in puts the diocese inside the reversed spot
echoing means the spot comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: a dot is a spot
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: Running a diocese while some spot keeps declining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'echoing' gives TOD, since an echo comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that runs to seed has gone past its best, so the idiom means deteriorate.

clue.text: Macabre morgues upset English

indicators.note: upset means the letters of morgues are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: English mortuaries knocked about make a ghastly scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Grisly and horrifying, especially to do with death.

clue.text: Travel document graduate left

parts.note: to pass is to get through, to graduate from one stage
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A graduate leaving the country with papers in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The official booklet that lets a citizen cross borders.

clue.text: Song about endless division in a state

indicators.note: about means the song goes round the other piece

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song

indicators.note: endless drops the last letter of the division word

parts.note: a zone is a division of an area

explanation.surface: A song about some endless split within one US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' just links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A south-western US state, an example of the class named.

clue.text: All-time low in Florida, numbers receding

indicators.note: receding says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A news line about Florida's figures falling to a record low.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of anything, borrowed from the point of the sky directly below the observer.

clue.text: Eating area Diane cleared, mostly

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diane

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word for cleared is dropped

parts.note: a business that cleared a sum netted it as profit

explanation.surface: Diane has cleared most of the dining corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleared' looks like tidying away plates but is earning as profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dining nook or alcove, off a kitchen.

clue.text: One's to touch down in Cuba, say

parts.note: I is one, so one's becomes I'S
to land is to touch down

explanation.surface: A traveller's plan to land in Cuba.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is an example of a piece of land surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Went round in a mini?

parts.note: reads as driving about in a small car, but is going about dressed in a short skirt; the verb also means went round

explanation.surface: Someone touring in a little car.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'mini' is the short skirt, not the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: avoided by going round, and wearing a skirt such as a miniskirt.

clue.text: Wrong base for cake

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A baker who used the wrong base for a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' is the mathematical constant e; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich, layered Central European gateau.

clue.text: Thump counter agitatedly

indicators.note: agitatedly says the letters of counter are shaken up

explanation.surface: Someone banging a shop counter in agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat soundly, as to thrash or defeat heavily.

clue.text: Love affair starts to affect my Open University revision

indicators.note: starts to means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A romance that is getting in the way of a student's Open University revision.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is a British distance-learning university.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for love, used in English for a romance, often a secret one.

clue.text: Deputy, without feeling, wrote anyhow

parts.note: numb means without sensation

indicators.note: anyhow means the letters of wrote are put in any old order

explanation.surface: A second-in-command writing carelessly and without emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal term for the second-in-command, the one just below the boss.

clue.text: I am butting in to discourage bore

indicators.note: butting in to means one piece is pushed inside another

parts.note: to deter is to discourage

explanation.surface: Someone interrupting to put off a tedious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a tiresome person but means the width of a gun barrel or pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The bore of a tube is its internal width measured straight across.

clue.text: Departs at this stage after a fix

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind a in the answer

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
here means at this point or stage

explanation.surface: A traveller leaving once something has been repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick fast or attach firmly, as glue does.
